Part IV then stops the story and lines up three answers — the worm was his fortune, not his disease; the worm was his disease, and poverty and sickness are still better than the death it would have brought; the worm was neither, because Liu was the worm and in losing it he killed himself — and the narrator says he does not know which is right, and that he has only listed them in imitation of the Didacticism of Chinese novelists. Every earlier pleasure of the tale, the heat, the grotesque cure, the comedy of the three waiting men, is retroactively put in question by that refusal. If the English lets any one answer win — by a sympathetic adjective for Liu, a sinister one for the monk, a wry or a mournful colouring in the final paragraphs — it has decided a case the text leaves open and become a fable about alcohol, or about quacks, or about genius destroyed by normality. None of those is this story.

crux.for_the_english: Keep the three answers parallel, evenly weighted and evenly plausible, in the same enumerating syntax. Keep the monk rude, abrupt and unexplained from first to last: he gives no greeting, answers Sun's questions ungraciously, states his diagnosis as fact. Do not make him a sage, a charlatan or a tempter. Keep Liu neither fool nor victim in the diction: he consents out of vanity, curiosity and a childish wish to show off a famous visitor, and the narrator reports those motives as coolly as he reports the weather.
crux.point: The narrator is a faux-scholarly intermediary, not a storyteller on the reader's side, and his asides are part of the mechanism.
crux.why: The tale is framed as a Chinese anecdote retold: it opens on the threshing-floor tableau with no explanation, breaks off to say of course this is not Japan but an incident at Changshan in China, flashes back with repeated deferrals ('the reason he lies there is this'), cross-refers to itself ('as said before'), quotes drinking and acreage in set Chinese phrases, digresses to compare Liu's ignorant submission to the treatment with ordinary people submitting to schooling, and signs off with a date. The erudition is real and also a pose; the citations and the numbered moral answers mimic a Chinese source the reader cannot check. That distance is what lets the impossible worm be reported like a case history.

open_questions.question: How far to reproduce the pose of scholarship in English: keep the capitalised foreign word 'Didacticism' as Akutagawa prints it, keep the quoted set phrases as quotations, and keep the self-references ('as said before') — or naturalise any of them? Naturalising is smoother and loses the frame.
open_questions.why_it_matters: These are the visible seams of the retelling. Cut or soften them and the story reads as an original fable; keep them stiffly and it reads as pastiche. The choice governs the whole register.

open_questions.question: Chinese names and measures in English form: Liu Dacheng, Sun, Changshan, Baodong temple, and 'three hundred mu' — Chinese readings, or the Japanese readings (Ryū Daisei and so on) through which a 1916 Japanese reader met them?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Akutagawa's China is a Japan-mediated, bookish China, closer to a Liaozhai retelling than to reportage. Fully sinicised names make the English more 'authentic' than the Japanese feels; Japanese readings make it opaque. Either is defensible; mixing them is not.

open_questions.question: The third answer's equation — Liu is the worm, the worm is Liu — reads as Buddhist-flavoured paradox and as a plain statement of identity. Should the English keep its aphoristic snap, at the cost of sounding like a Zen epigram Akutagawa may be parodying along with the moralists?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the answer most readers remember, and the one most likely to be mistaken for the author's own verdict. Its tone decides whether the ending feels profound or deliberately over-neat.

reading.reading:
Begin from the crux, because everything in the manner serves it. Part I is a held tableau: three men in killing heat, one of them naked, bound hand and foot with cord, lying on his back with an unglazed jar at his head, saying nothing, barely moving, like clay statues in a Guandi temple. The text withholds every reason for this and makes the reader wait in the heat with them. Part II supplies the reasons, slowly, through vanity and gossip rather than through any urgency of illness — Liu, it is made clear, did not feel ill and had never once been drunk. Part III narrows to a single body: sweat running into eyes that cannot be wiped, skin prickling as if pulled in all directions at once, thirst sharpened by the smell of wine from the jar, then the thing moving up the oesophagus, now like an earthworm, now like a gecko shifting its weight, now slipping out like a loach. Part IV jumps three years in a paragraph and turns a strange cure into destitution, then into a seminar. Keep those four movements distinct in English. Do not let the opening tableau acquire explanatory connectives it does not have, do not let the flashback hurry, do not let the expulsion scene be summarised, and do not let the last section slow into elegy.

The sound is learned and sensuous at once. The heat writing of Part I is dense with Sino-Japanese compounds and similes — roof tiles dully reflecting light like lead, cloud-peaks like hail roasted in an earthen pan, swallows' nests that might steam the chicks inside — and it returns in Part III as bodily sensation, so that the weather of the first page becomes the torture of the third. English that varies or thins this vocabulary breaks the link. Keep the repetitions that build it: heat, silence, stillness, the jar, the smell of wine growing minute by minute. The unglazed jar and Sun's white-feather fan are introduced as unidentified objects and identified later, in the narrator's own time; a translation that names their contents or owner early has rationalised the structure away. Dialogue, by contrast, is short and flat, the monk's especially, and should stay flat against the narrator's elaboration.

Names for the fluent failures to resist, in the house's terms: clarification — explaining what the wine worm is before or beyond the swimming thing in the jar, or glossing the monk's method as sympathetic magic; ennoblement — making the Chinese setting picturesquely exotic, or the ending wise; impoverishment — 'bug' or 'parasite' for a creature the text presents with mouth, eyes and an appetite; destroying the network of repeated words — varying wine, worm, drink, heat where the Japanese insists on them; and above all rationalisation of the close, where the three answers must remain a list the narrator declines to adjudicate, capped by his confession of ignorance and the dated sign-off, which should land as dryly in English as it does in Japanese. The monk's cure works exactly as promised and ruins the patient, and the text's position is that both halves of that sentence are simply true. Translate so that the reader, like the people of Changshan, is left repeating the question.
reading.say: The reading above is complete. The three open questions are recommended to the editor as forks, with the first — how visibly to keep the scholarly pose — settled before drafting, since it determines register throughout.

voice_takes.label: Dry, exact, faintly antiquarian — a case history told deadpan, the grotesque left to do its own work.
Warmer and more novelistic — Liu's decline given pathos, the comedy broadened.
Flatter and more modern — shorter sentences, contemporary diction, the Chinese apparatus kept minimal.

release.title: 酒虫

casual.en: I
casual.ja: 一
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: It is a heat unknown in recent years. Wherever one looks, the roof-tiles of the mud-plastered houses reflect the sunlight dully, like lead, so that even the swallows' nests hung beneath them seem, at this rate, like to steam the chicks and eggs within to death just as they are. What is more, every field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the heat rising from the earth, and there is not one thing that, for all its greenness, is not wilted. The sky seen above those fields, too, whether from the warm vapours of these last days, the air near the ground, though clear, hangs thick and turbid, and here and there the piled clouds, like hail parched in an earthen pan, mere shapes, float in clumps. — The tale of the "wine worm" begins with three men who in this weather have gone out of their way to be upon a threshing-floor in the blazing sun.
casual.ja: 近年にない暑さである。どこを見ても、泥で固めた家々の屋根瓦が、鉛のやうに鈍く日の光を反射して、その下に懸けてある燕の巣さへ、この塩梅では中にゐる雛や卵を、そのまゝ蒸殺してしまふかと思はれる。まして、畑と云ふ畑は、麻でも黍でも、皆、土いきれにぐつたりと頭をさげて、何一つ、青いなりに、萎れてゐないものはない。その畑の上に見える空も、この頃の温気に中てられたせいか、地上に近い大気は、晴れながら、どんよりと濁つて、その所々に、霰を炮烙で煎つたやうな、形ばかりの雲の峰が、つぶつぶと浮かんでゐる。――「酒虫」の話は、この陽気に、わざ〳〵炎天の打麦場へ出てゐる、三人の男で始まるのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Strangely, one of them lies stark naked on his back on the bare ground. What is more, for some reason or other, hand and foot he is wound round and round with thin cord. Yet the man himself shows no sign of suffering it as a hardship. He is short, of good colour, somehow giving a sense of dull heaviness, a man fat as a pig. Then a handy-sized unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow, but what is inside that, too, is not known.
casual.ja: 不思議な事に、その中の一人は、素裸で、仰向けに地面へ寝ころんでゐる。おまけに、どう云ふ訳だか、細引で、手も足もぐる〳〵巻にされてゐる。が格別当人は、それを苦に病んでゐる容子もない。背の低い、血色の好い、どことなく鈍重と云ふ感じを起させる、豚のやうに肥つた男である。それから手ごろな素焼の瓶が一つ、この男の枕もとに置いてあるが、これも中に何がはいつてゐるのだか、わからない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Another is a monk of strikingly antique aspect, in a yellow robe with a small bronze ring hung from his ear. His skin is remarkably black in colour, and to judge from his curled hair and beard, he would seem to be a man come from somewhere west of the Congling Mountains. Until now he has been patiently flourishing a red-handled shubi to drive off the horseflies and flies that would settle upon the naked man, but he appears at last to have tired a little, and now he has come over beside the unglazed earthen jar and squats there with an air of importance, in the attitude of a turkey.
casual.ja: もう一人は、黄色い法衣を着て、耳に小さな青銅の環をさげた、一見、象貌の奇古な沙門である。皮膚の色が並はづれて黒い上に、髪や鬚の縮れてゐる所を見ると、どうも葱嶺の西からでも来た人間らしい。これはさつきから根気よく、朱柄の麈尾をふりふり、裸の男にたからうとする虻や蠅を追つてゐたが、流石に少しくたびれたと見えて、今では、例の素焼の瓶の側へ来て、七面鳥のやうな恰好をしながら、勿体らしくしやがんでゐる。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The last stands far apart from these two, under the eaves of a thatched hut in the corner of the threshing-floor. This man sports only a token beard, like a rat's tail, on the tip of his chin, and wears a black cloth gown long enough to hide his heels, with a tea-brown sash whose knot hangs sloppily. To judge from the manner in which from time to time he handles a fan made of white birds' feathers with great care, he is most likely a Confucian scholar or something of the kind.
casual.ja: あとの一人は、この二人からずつと離れて、打麦場の隅にある草房の軒下に立つてゐる。この男は、頤の先に、鼠の尻尾のやうな髯を、申訳だけに生やして、踵が隠れる程長い皁布衫に、結目をだらしなく垂らした茶褐帯と云ふ拵へである。白い鳥の羽で製つた団扇を、時々大事さうに使つてゐる容子では、多分、儒者か何かにちがひない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: All three, as if by agreement, keep their mouths shut. What is more, they hardly so much as move, as though they took extraordinary interest in something now about to happen, and for that reason were all holding their breath.
casual.ja: この三人が三人とも、云ひ合せたやうに、口を噤んでゐる。その上、碌に身動きさへもしない、何か、これから起らうとする事に、非常な興味でも持つてゐて、その為に、皆、息をひそめてゐるのではないかと思はれる。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: It must be just noon. Whether because even the dogs are taking their midday nap, not a single bark is heard. The hemp and millet that enclose the threshing-floor shine their green leaves in the sun and rest hushed and utterly still. And the sky seen beyond them, stifling with heat over its whole face, trails heat-haze, so that even the piled clouds seem to be panting in this dry spell. Look where one will, the only things that seem to breathe are these three men. And those three keep silence like the clay images enshrined in a Guandi temple....
casual.ja: 日は正に、亭午であらう。犬も午睡をしてゐるせいか、吠える声一つ聞えない。打麦場を囲んでゐる麻や黍も、青い葉を日に光らせて、ひつそりかんと静まつてゐる。それから、その末に見える空も、一面に、熱くるしく、炎靄をたゞよはせて、雲の峰さへもこの旱に、肩息をついてゐるのかと、疑はれる。見渡した所、息が通つてゐるらしいのは、この三人の男の外にない。さうして、その三人が又、関帝廟に安置してある、泥塑の像のやうに沈黙を守つてゐる。……
casual.label: house-checked

notes.body: Guandi is the deified general Guan Yu, worshipped in temples filled with life-size clay figures; the point is stock-still silence.
notes.span: like the clay images enshrined in a Guandi temple

casual.en: Of course, this is no tale of Japan. — It is what happened one summer on the threshing-floor of a Liu at a place called Changshan in China.
casual.ja: 勿論、日本の話ではない。――支那の長山と云ふ所にある劉氏の打麦場で、或年の夏、起つた出来事である。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: II
casual.ja: 二
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The man lying naked in the blazing sun is the master of this threshing-floor, surnamed Liu, named Dacheng, one of the leading rich men of Changshan. This man's sole diversion is the drinking of wine, and from morning he has scarcely ever been known to part from the cup. And that, as the phrase has it, "Each time he drinks alone, he empties a whole jar" — a measure of wine beyond the common run of men. Though, as said before, "Fields by the walls, three hundred mu, half sown with millet," so there is not the least fear that his drinking should encumber his estate.
casual.ja: 裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるのは、この打麦場の主人で、姓は劉、名は大成と云ふ、長山では、屈指の素封家の一人である。この男の道楽は、酒を飲む一方で、朝から、殆、盃を離したと云ふ事がない。それも、「独酌する毎に輒、一甕を尽す」と云ふのだから、人並をはづれた酒量である。尤も前にも云つたやうに、「負郭の田三百畝、半は黍を種う」と云ふので、飲の為に家産が累はされるやうな惧は、万々ない。
casual.label: house-checked

notes.body: A mu is a Chinese measure of land, a fraction of an acre that varied by time and place; three hundred mu means a large estate.

casual.en: Why it is that he lies naked in the blazing sun has a history behind it, and it is this. — That day Liu was together with Sun Sensei, his companion in drinking (this is the scholar who held the white-feather fan), in a well-aired room, leaning against a bamboo-wife bolster and playing out a game on the board, when the maidservant, a yahuan, came and said, "A monk who says he is staying at the Hodoji temple or somewhere has just come, and says he must by all means see the master. What shall I do?"
casual.ja: それが、何故、裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるかと云ふと、それには、かう云ふ因縁がある。――その日、劉が、同じ飲仲間の孫先生と一しよに（これが、白羽扇を持つてゐた儒者である。）風通しのいゝ室で、竹婦人に靠れながら、棋局を闘はせてゐると、召使ひの丫鬟が来て、「唯今、宝幢寺とかにゐると云ふ、坊さんが御見えになりまして、是非、御主人に御目にかゝりたいと申しますが、いかゞ致しませう。」と云ふ。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "What, the Hodoji?" So saying, Liu blinked his small eyes as if dazzled, then, raising his fat body that looked hot in itself, ordered, "Then show him in here." Then, with a glance at Sun Sensei's face, he added, "It will be that monk, I suppose."
casual.ja: 「なに、宝幢寺？」かう云つて、劉は小さな眼を、まぶしさうに、しばたたいたが、やがて、暑さうに肥つた体を起しながら、「では、こゝへ御通し申せ。」と云ひつけた。それから、孫先生の顔をちよいと見て「大方あの坊主でせう。」とつけ加へた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The monk at the Hodoji temple is a barbarian monk come from the Western Regions. Since he both lends a hand at healing and practises the arts of the bedchamber, his fame stands high in these parts. Rumours all but miraculous are rife — that Zhang San's black cataract suddenly turned toward recovery, that Li Si's eunuch-like illness was healed on the spot, and the like. — Both men had heard these rumours. What business could have brought that barbarian monk now, taking the trouble to come all the way to Liu's? Liu, for his part, had no recollection whatever of having sent to fetch him.
casual.ja: 宝幢寺にゐる坊主と云ふのは、西域から来た蛮僧である。これが、医療も加へれば、房術も施すと云ふので、この界隈では、評判が高い。たとへば、張三の黒内障が、忽、快方に向つたとか、李四の病閹が、即座に平癒したとか、殆、奇蹟に近い噂が盛に行はれてゐるのである。――この噂は、二人とも聞いてゐた。その蛮僧が、今、何の用で、わざわざ、劉の所へ出むいて来たのであらう。勿論、劉の方から、迎へにやつた覚えなどは、全然ない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: To note it in passing, Liu was not at all a man who delighted in visitors. But when he already had one visitor with him, and a new visitor came, he would generally receive him gladly. He had a childish vanity of the sort that might be described as showing off the fact of having a visitor before a visitor. Besides, today's barbarian monk was at this time the talk everywhere. He was by no means a visitor one would be ashamed to meet. — Liu's motives in saying he would meet him lay roughly here.
casual.ja: 序に云つて置くが、劉は、一体、来客を悦ぶやうな男ではない。が、他に一人、来客がある場合に、新来の客が来たとなると、大抵ならば、快く会つてやる。客の手前、客のあるのを自慢するとでも云つたらよささうな、小供らしい虚栄心を持つてゐるからである。それに、今日の蛮僧は、この頃、どこででも評判になつてゐる。決して、会つて恥しいやうな客ではない。――劉が会はうと云ひ出した動機は、大体こんな所にあつたのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "What business can he have?"
casual.ja: 「何の用でせう。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Alms-seeking, most likely. He will be asking for some charity, I suppose."
casual.ja: 「まづ、物貰ひですな。信施でもしてくれと云ふのでせう。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: While the two were talking such things over between them, presently there entered, guided in by the yahuan, a monk of strange aspect, tall and with eyes like cut violet quartz. He wore a yellow robe, his grown-out curling hair hanging tiresomely over his shoulders. Still holding his red-handled shubi, he planted himself heavily in the middle of the room. He offered no greeting, nor did he speak.
casual.ja: こんな事を、二人で話してゐる内に、やがて、丫鬟の案内で、はいつて来たのを見ると、背の高い、紫石稜のやうな眼をした、異形な沙門である。黄色い法衣を着て、その肩に、縮れた髪の伸びたのを、うるささうに垂らしてゐる。それが、朱柄の麈尾を持つたまゝ、のつそり室のまん中に立つた。挨拶もしなければ、口もきかない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Liu hesitated for a while, but as that somehow grew unsettling to him, he ventured, "Have you some business with me?"
casual.ja: 劉は、しばらく、ためらつてゐたが、その内に、それが何となく、不安になつて来たので「何か御用かな。」と訊いて見た。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Whereupon the barbarian monk said, "You are the one, I take it, who is fond of wine."
casual.ja: すると、蛮僧が云つた。「あなたでせうな、酒が好きなのは。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "I am." The question was so abrupt that Liu, as he gave his vague answer, looked toward Sun Sensei as if seeking rescue. Sun Sensei, with a composed air, went on laying stones on the board by himself. He showed no disposition to take any part.
casual.ja: 「さやう。」劉は、あまり問が唐突なので、曖昧な返事をしながら、救を求めるやうに、孫先生の方を見た。孫先生は、すまして、独りで、盤面に石を下してゐる。まるで、取り合ふ容子はない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "You are afflicted with a rare disease. Are you aware of it?" the barbarian monk said, as if to make sure. Liu, hearing of a disease, made a dubious face, and, stroking his bamboo wife,
casual.ja: 「あなたは、珍しい病に罹つて御出になる。それを御存知ですかな。」蛮僧は念を押すやうに、かう云つた。劉は、病と聞いたので、けげんな顔をして、竹婦人を撫でながら、
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "A disease — you say?"
casual.ja: 「病――ですかな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "It is."
casual.ja: 「さうです。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "No, since I was a child..." As Liu was about to say something more, the barbarian monk cut him off.
casual.ja: 「いや、幼少の時から……」劉が何か云はうとすると、蛮僧はそれを遮つて、
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "However much wine you drink, you never get drunk."
casual.ja: 「酒を飲まれても、酔ひますまいな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "..." Liu stared at the man's face and shut his mouth. In fact, however much wine this man drank, he had never once been drunk.
casual.ja: 「……」劉は、ぢろぢろ、相手の顔を見ながら、口を噤んでしまつた。実際この男は、いくら酒を飲んでも、酔つた事がないのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "That is the proof of the disease," the barbarian monk went on with a faint smile. "There is a wine worm in your belly. Unless it is removed, this disease will not be cured. This poor monk has come to cure your disease."
casual.ja: 「それが、病の証拠ですよ。」蛮僧は、うす笑をしながら、語をついで、「腹中に酒虫がゐる。それを除かないと、この病は癒りません。貧道は、あなたの病を癒しに来たのです。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Can it be cured?" Liu cried out before he knew it, in an uncertain voice. And he was ashamed of himself for it.
casual.ja: 「癒りますかな。」劉は思はず覚束なさうな声を出した。さうして、自分でそれを恥ぢた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "It can be cured, which is why I have come."
casual.ja: 「癒ればこそ、来ましたが。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Then Sun Sensei, who had till now listened in silence to the exchange of questions and answers, suddenly put in a word.
casual.ja: すると、今まで、黙つて、問答を聞いてゐた孫先生が、急に語を挟んだ。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Will you use some medicine?"
casual.ja: 「何か、薬でも御用ひか。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "No, there is no need to use medicine or the like," the barbarian monk answered ungraciously.
casual.ja: 「いや、薬なぞは用ひるまでもありません。」蛮僧は不愛想に、かう答へた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Sun Sensei by nature despised the two teachings of the Daoists and the Buddhists almost without reason. Hence he had rarely ever spoken a word when in company with a Daoist priest or a Buddhist monk. That he had now taken a sudden fancy to intervene was wholly because his interest had been stirred by the words wine worm, for Sensei, who loved wine, hearing this, had grown a little uneasy lest there be a wine worm in his own belly as well. On hearing the barbarian monk's grudging answer, however, he suddenly felt as if he himself had been made a fool of, so with a slight grimace he began once more in silence to lay the pieces down as before. And at the same time he thought inwardly how foolish of his host Liu to receive such an arrogant monk.
casual.ja: 孫先生は、元来、道仏の二教を殆、無理由に軽蔑してゐる。だから、道士とか僧侶とかと一しよになつても、口をきいた事は滅多にない。それが、今ふと口を出す気になつたのは、全く酒虫と云ふ語の興味に動かされたからで、酒の好きな先生は、これを聞くと、自分の腹の中にも、酒虫がゐはしないかと、聊、不安になつて来たのである。所が、蛮僧の不承不承な答を聞くと、急に、自分が莫迦にされたやうな気がしたので、先生はちよいと顔をしかめながら、又元の通り、黙々として棋子を下しはじめた。さうして、それと同時に、内心、こんな横柄な坊主に会つたり何ぞする主人の劉を、莫迦げてゐると思ひ出した。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Liu, for his part, of course paid no heed to any of this.
casual.ja: 劉の方では、勿論そんな事には頓着しない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Then will you use needles?"
casual.ja: 「では、針でも使ひますかな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "No, it is a thing of still less trouble."
casual.ja: 「なに、もつと造作のない事です。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Then is it a spell?"
casual.ja: 「では呪ですかな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "No, nor is it a spell."
casual.ja: 「いや、呪でもありません。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: After repeating such talk, the barbarian monk briefly explained the cure to them. — By his account, one had only to strip naked and keep still in the sun. To Liu this seemed a very easy matter. If so small a thing would cure him, there was nothing better than to be cured. And, though he was not aware of it, he was also a little moved by curiosity at undergoing the barbarian monk's treatment.
casual.ja: かう云ふ会話を繰返した末に、蛮僧は、簡単に、その療法を説明して聞かせた。――それによるに、唯、裸になつて、日向にぢつとしてゐさへすればよいと云ふのである。劉には、それが、甚、容易な事のやうに思はれた。その位の事で癒るなら、癒して貰ふのに越した事はない。その上、意識してはゐなかつたが、蛮僧の治療を受けると云ふ点で、好奇心も少しは動いてゐた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: So at last Liu bowed his head of his own accord, and it came to this: "Then I must ask you to cure me, if you please." — Such is the reason why Liu lies naked upon the threshing-floor in the blazing sun.
casual.ja: そこでとうとう、劉も、こつちから頭を下げて、「では、どうか一つ、癒して頂きませう。」と云ふ事になつた。――劉が、裸で、炎天の打麦場にねころんでゐるのには、かう云ふ謂れが、あるのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Thereupon, saying he must not stir, the barbarian monk wound Liu's body round and round with thin cord. Then, bidding one of the servants, he had an unglazed earthen jar with wine in it brought to Liu's pillow. That Sun Sensei, the good friend of the wine-mound, should in the course of things have come to stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
casual.ja: すると蛮僧は、身動きをしてはいけないと云ふので、劉の体を細引で、ぐるぐる巻にした。それから、僮僕の一人に云ひつけて、酒を入れた素焼の瓶を一つ、劉の枕もとへ持つて来させた。当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: What sort of thing the wine worm is, what happens when it is no longer in the belly, and what the jar of wine at the pillow is for, no one knows but the barbarian monk alone. To put it so, Liu, who has gone out naked into the blazing sun knowing nothing, may seem very heedless, but what ordinary men do when they receive schooling and the like is in truth for the most part the same sort of thing.
casual.ja: 酒虫と云ふ物が、どんな物だか、それが腹の中にゐなくなると、どうなるのだか、枕もとにある酒の瓶は、何にするつもりなのだか、それを知つてゐるのは、蛮僧の外に一人もない。かう云ふと、何も知らずに、炎天へ裸で出てゐる劉は、甚、迂濶なやうに思はれるが、普通の人間が、学校の教育などをうけるのも、実は大抵、これと同じやうな事をしてゐるのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: III
casual.ja: 三
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: It is hot. Sweat comes welling up with a prickle across the brow, and when it seems to have beaded it comes trickling, lukewarm, toward the eyes. As ill luck will have it, he is bound with thin cord, so of course there is no putting out a hand to wipe it. He tries moving his neck to turn the course of the sweat aside, but at that instant a violent dizziness seems ready to come on, so to his disappointment he gave up this plan too. All the while the sweat without ceremony wets the eyelids and, passing from the side of the nose round the mouth, runs on down beneath the chin. It is disagreeable beyond measure.
casual.ja: 暑い。額へ汗がぢりぢりと湧いて来て、それが玉になつたかと思ふと、つうつと生暖く、眼の方へ流れて来る。生憎、細引でしばられてゐるから、手を出して拭ふ訳には、勿論行かない。そこで、首を動かして、汗の進路を変へやうとすると、その途端に、はげしく眩暈がしさうな気がしたので、残念ながら、この計画も亦、見合せる事にした。その中に、汗は遠慮なく、眶をぬらして、鼻の側から口許をまはりながら、頤の下まで流れて行く。気味が悪い事夥しい。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Until then he had lain with eyes open, staring hard at the sky seared white and the hemp-field with its drooping leaves, but once the sweat began to pour without restraint even that had to be given up. It was then that Liu learned for the first time that sweat stings when it gets into the eyes. And so, with the face of a sheep in the slaughterhouse, meekly shutting his eyes and lying still while the sun beats down upon him, now in turn the skin of the upper parts, face or body alike, began gradually to feel a certain pain. Across every inch of skin something tugs in every direction at once, and the skin has no give in it at all. A pain that might best be described as a tingling everywhere. This is not the misery of prickly heat. Liu began to find it hateful that he had taken the barbarian monk's cure.
casual.ja: それまでは、眼を開いて、白く焦された空や、葉をたらした麻畑を、まじ〳〵と眺めてゐたが、汗が無暗に流れるやうになつてからは、それさへ断念しなければならなくなつた。劉は、この時、始めて、汗が眼にはいると、しみるものだと云ふ事を、知つたのである。そこで、屠所の羊の様な顔をして、神妙に眼をつぶりながら、ぢつと日に照りつけられてゐると、今度は、顔と云はず体と云はず、上になつてゐる部分の皮膚が、次第に或痛みを感じるやうになつて来た。皮膚の全面に、あらゆる方向へ動かうとする力が働いてゐるが、皮膚自身は、それに対して、毫も弾力を持つてゐない。それでどこもかしこも、ぴり〳〵する――とでも説明したら、よからうと思ふ痛みである。これは、汗所の苦しさではない。劉は、少し蛮僧の治療をうけたのが、忌々しくなつて来た。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: However, thinking it over afterwards, this was still the part that was less painful. — Before long his throat grows parched. Liu too knows the story of how Cao Mengde, or someone, cured the thirst of his soldiers by telling them there was a plum grove ahead. But now, picture as he will the sweet sourness of plums in his mind, his thirst is not a whit the less for it. He moves his jaw about, he bites his tongue, yet inside his mouth still keeps its heat. That too might still have been somewhat easier to bear, had there not been the unglazed earthen jar at his pillow. From the mouth of the jar the rich fragrant smell of wine comes without break to assail his nose. And, though it may be fancy, he even feels that smell growing stronger with every minute. Thinking at least to look at the jar, Liu opened his eyes. Glancing upward, he sees the mouth of the jar and something like half of its amply bulging body. That alone is what he sees, but at the same time there rises before Liu's imagination the sight of wine the colour of gold brimming in the dim interior of that jar. Before he knew it he had licked his cracked lips with his dry tongue, yet there is no sign at all of saliva springing. Even the sweat, dried now by the sun, no longer flows as before.
casual.ja: しかし、これは、後になつて考へて見ると、まだ苦しくない方の部だつたのである。――そのうちに、喉が渇いて来た。劉も、曹孟徳か誰かが、前路に梅林ありと云つて、軍士の渇を医したと云ふ事は知つてゐる。が、今の場合、いくら、梅子の甘酸を念頭に浮べて見ても、喉の渇く事は、少しも前と変りがない。頤を動かして見たり、舌を噛んで見たりしたが、口の中は依然として熱を持つてゐる。それも、枕もとの素焼の瓶がなかつたら、まだ幾分でも、我慢がし易かつたのに違ひない。所が、瓶の口からは、芬々たる酒香が、間断なく、劉の鼻を襲つて来る。しかも、気のせいか、その酒香が、一分毎に、益々高くなつて来るやうな心もちさへする。劉は、せめて、瓶だけでも見ようと思つて、眼をあけた。上眼を使つて見ると、瓶の口と、応揚にふくれた胴の半分ばかりが、眼にはいる。眼にはいるのは、それだけであるが、同時に、劉の想像には、その瓶のうす暗い内部に、黄金のやうな色をした酒のなみ〳〵と湛へてゐる容子が、浮んで来た。思はず、ひびの出来た唇を、乾いた舌で舐めまはして見たが、唾の湧く気色は、更にない。汗さへ今では、日に干されて、前のやうには、流れなくなつてしまつた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Then a violent dizziness came, two or three times in succession. The headache has not abated since some time ago. In his heart Liu thought the barbarian monk ever more hateful. And he thought too why a man of his standing should have let such a fellow talk him round into suffering so foolish a torment. Meanwhile his throat grows ever more parched. His chest turns strangely queasy. He can no longer bear it, to lie still. So at last Liu resolved, and, panting, opened his mouth, meaning to ask the barbarian monk at his pillow to call off the cure. —
casual.ja: すると、はげしい眩暈が、つづいて、二三度起つた。頭痛はさつきから、しつきりなしにしてゐる。劉は、心の中で愈、蛮僧を怨めしく思つた。それから又何故、自分ともあるものが、あんな人間の口車に乗つて、こんな莫迦げた苦しみをするのだらうとも思つた。そのうちに、喉は、益々、渇いて来る。胸は妙にむかついて来る。もう我慢にも、ぢつとしてはゐられない。そこで劉はとう〳〵思切つて、枕もとの蛮僧に、療治の中止を申込むつもりで、喘ぎながら、口を開いた。――
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: At that very instant. Liu began to feel an indescribable lump creeping little by little from his chest up toward his throat. At one moment it seems to writhe like an earthworm, at another to edge along little by little like a gecko. In any case some soft thing, soft as it is, comes wriggling and pressing up the gullet. And at last, when it has forced its way past beneath the Adam's apple, all at once it slips slick out of the dark place like a loach or something and flies outward with force.
casual.ja: すると、その途端である。劉は、何とも知れない塊が、少しづゝ胸から喉へ這ひ上つて来るのを感じ出した。それが或は蚯蚓のやうに、蠕動してゐるかと思ふと、或は守宮のやうに、少しづゝ居ざつてゐるやうでもある。兎に角或柔い物が、柔いなりに、むづりむづりと、食道を上へせり上つて来るのである。さうしてとうとうしまひに、それが、喉仏の下を、無理にすりぬけたと思ふと、今度はいきなり、鰌か何かのやうにぬるりと暗い所をぬけ出して、勢よく外へとんで出た。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: And with that, from the quarter of the familiar unglazed earthen jar, there sounded a plop, as of something falling into wine.
casual.ja: と、その拍子に、例の素焼の瓶の方で、ぽちやりと、何か酒の中へ落ちるやうな音がした。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Upon this the barbarian monk suddenly heaved himself up from where he had settled and began to undo the thin cord wound about Liu's body. The wine worm is out, so be at ease, is what he means.
casual.ja: すると、蛮僧が、急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて、劉の体にかゝつてゐる、細引を解きはじめた。もう、酒虫が出たから、安心しろと云ふのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Has it come out?" Liu said as if groaning, lifting his swimming head, and out of sheer curiosity, forgetting even his thirst, crawled naked to the side of the jar. At this, Sun Sensei too, shading himself from the sun with his white-feather fan, came hurrying toward the two. When all three together peered into the jar, a thing like a small salamander, flesh-coloured as red clay, was swimming in the wine. In length perhaps three sun. It had a mouth, and it had eyes. As it swam it seemed somehow to be drinking the wine. At the sight of it Liu felt suddenly sick. ...
casual.ja: 「出ましたかな。」劉は、呻くやうにかう云つて、ふらふらする頭を起しながら、物珍しさの余り、喉の渇いたのも忘れて、裸のまま、瓶の側へ這ひよつた。それと見ると、孫先生も、白羽扇で日をよけながら、急いで、二人の方へやつて来る。さて、三人揃つて瓶の中を覗きこむと、肉の色が朱泥に似た、小さな山椒魚のやうなものが、酒の中を泳いでゐる。長さは、三寸ばかりであらう。口もあれば、眼もある。どうやら、泳ぎながら、酒を飲んでゐるらしい。劉はこれを見ると、急に胸が悪くなつた。……
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: IV
casual.ja: 四
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The effect of the barbarian monk's treatment appeared at once. From that day Liu Dacheng abruptly could drink no more wine. Now he will not bear even to smell it, they say. Strangely, from that time Liu's health began to fail little by little. This year is three years since he spat out the wine worm, and no trace remains of the round, fat figure of former years. Skin of poor lustre, greasy still, wraps the harsh bones of his face, and frost-touched hair at the temples survives only faintly, and in a year none knows how many times he takes to his bed, they say.
casual.ja: 蛮僧の治療の効は、覿面に現れた。劉大成は、その日から、ぱつたり酒が飲めなくなつたのである。今は、匂を嗅ぐのも、嫌だと云ふ。所が、不思議な事に、劉の健康が、それから、少しづつ、衰へて来た。今年で、酒虫を吐いてから、三年になるが、往年の丸丸と肥つてゐた俤は、何処にもない。色光沢の悪い皮膚が、脂じみたまま、険しい顔の骨を包んで、霜に侵された双髩が、纔に、顳顬の上に、残つてゐるばかり、一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位ださうである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Yet it was not Liu's health alone that has failed since then. His estate too has declined headlong, and now of the fields by the walls counted as three hundred mu, most have passed into other hands. Liu himself, perforce, has taken the plough in unpractised hands and passes his days, day by day, in cheerlessness.
casual.ja: しかし、それ以来、衰へたのは、劉の健康ばかりではない。劉の家産も亦とんとん拍子に傾いて、今では、三百畝を以て数へた負郭の田も、多くは人の手に渡つた。劉自身も、余儀なく、馴れない手に鋤を執つて、佗しいその日その日を送つてゐるのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Since spitting out the wine worm, why has Liu's health failed? Why has the estate declined — once you set the spitting-out of the wine worm side by side with Liu's later ruin as cause and effect, it is a question anyone would ask. In fact this question has been repeated by people of every occupation living in Changshan, and from the mouths of those people answers of every kind have been given. The three answers set down here are in truth no more than the most representative chosen from among them.
casual.ja: 酒虫を吐いて以来、何故、劉の健康が衰へたか。何故、家産が傾いたか――酒虫を吐いたと云ふ事と、劉のその後の零落とを、因果の関係に並べて見る以上、これは、誰にでも起りやすい疑問である。現にこの疑問は、長山に住んでゐる、あらゆる職業の人人によつて繰返され、且、それらの人人の口から、あらゆる種類の答を与へられた。今、ここに挙げる三つの答も、実はその中から、最、代表的なものを選んだのに過ぎない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: First answer. The wine worm was Liu's fortune, and not Liu's disease. Through chancing to meet with a benighted barbarian monk, he willingly came to lose this heaven-given fortune.
casual.ja: 第一の答。酒虫は、劉の福であつて、劉の病ではない。偶、暗愚の蛮僧に遇つた為に、好んで、この天与の福を失ふやうな事になつたのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Second answer. The wine worm was Liu's disease, and not Liu's fortune. For to drain a whole jar at a single drinking is quite beyond what an ordinary man can conceive. Had the wine worm not been removed, Liu must soon have died, without doubt. That being so, poverty and sickness arriving each in turn should rather be called happiness for Liu.
casual.ja: 第二の答。酒虫は、劉の病であつて、劉の福ではない。何故と云へば、一飲一甕を尽すなどと云ふ事は、到底、常人の考へられない所だからである。そこで、もし酒虫を除かなかつたなら、劉は必久しからずして、死んだのに相違ない。して見ると、貧病、迭に至るのも、寧劉にとつては、幸福と云ふべきである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Third answer. The wine worm was neither Liu's disease nor Liu's fortune. Liu from of old drank nothing but wine. If wine is taken from Liu's life, afterwards nothing remains. That being so, Liu is the wine worm, the wine worm is Liu. Therefore Liu's parting with the wine worm is the same as killing himself. In short, from the day he could drink wine no more, Liu is Liu and yet is not Liu. If Liu himself was already gone, that the health and estate of the Liu of former days should have been lost would be only natural.
casual.ja: 第三の答。酒虫は、劉の病でもなければ、劉の福でもない。劉は、昔から酒ばかり飲んでゐた。劉の一生から酒を除けば、後には、何も残らない。して見ると、劉は即酒虫、酒虫は即劉である。だから、劉が酒虫を去つたのは自ら己を殺したのも同前である。つまり、酒が飲めなくなつた日から、劉は劉にして、劉ではない。劉自身が既になくなつてゐたとしたら、昔日の劉の健康なり家産なりが、失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Which of these answers comes nearest to the mark, I myself do not know. I have merely listed such moral judgments at the end of this tale, in imitation of the *Didacticism* of Chinese novelists.
casual.ja: これらの答の中で、どれが、最よく、当を得てゐるか、それは自分にもわからない。自分は、唯、支那の小説家の Didacticism に倣つて、かう云ふ道徳的な判断を、この話の最後に、列挙して見たまでゝある。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: — Fourth Month of the Fifth Year —
casual.ja: ――五年四月――
casual.label: house-checked

curious.en: I
curious.ja: 一
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: It is a heat unknown in recent years. Wherever one looks, the roof-tiles of the mud-plastered houses reflect the sunlight dully, like lead, so that even the swallows' nests hung beneath them seem, at this rate, like to steam the chicks and eggs within to death just as they are. What is more, every field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the heat rising from the earth, and there is not one thing that, for all its greenness, is not wilted. The sky seen above those fields, too, whether from the warm vapours of these last days, the air near the ground, though clear, hangs thick and turbid, and here and there the piled clouds, like hail parched in an earthen pan, mere shapes, float in clumps. — The tale of the "wine worm" begins with three men who in this weather have gone out of their way to be upon a threshing-floor in the blazing sun.
curious.ja: 近年にない暑さである。どこを見ても、泥で固めた家々の屋根瓦が、鉛のやうに鈍く日の光を反射して、その下に懸けてある燕の巣さへ、この塩梅では中にゐる雛や卵を、そのまゝ蒸殺してしまふかと思はれる。まして、畑と云ふ畑は、麻でも黍でも、皆、土いきれにぐつたりと頭をさげて、何一つ、青いなりに、萎れてゐないものはない。その畑の上に見える空も、この頃の温気に中てられたせいか、地上に近い大気は、晴れながら、どんよりと濁つて、その所々に、霰を炮烙で煎つたやうな、形ばかりの雲の峰が、つぶつぶと浮かんでゐる。――「酒虫」の話は、この陽気に、わざ〳〵炎天の打麦場へ出てゐる、三人の男で始まるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Strangely, one of them lies stark naked on his back on the bare ground. What is more, for some reason or other, hand and foot he is wound round and round with thin cord. Yet the man himself shows no sign of suffering it as a hardship. He is short, of good colour, somehow giving a sense of dull heaviness, a man fat as a pig. Then a handy-sized unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow, but what is inside that, too, is not known.
curious.ja: 不思議な事に、その中の一人は、素裸で、仰向けに地面へ寝ころんでゐる。おまけに、どう云ふ訳だか、細引で、手も足もぐる〳〵巻にされてゐる。が格別当人は、それを苦に病んでゐる容子もない。背の低い、血色の好い、どことなく鈍重と云ふ感じを起させる、豚のやうに肥つた男である。それから手ごろな素焼の瓶が一つ、この男の枕もとに置いてあるが、これも中に何がはいつてゐるのだか、わからない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Another is a monk of strikingly antique aspect, in a yellow robe with a small bronze ring hung from his ear. His skin is remarkably black in colour, and to judge from his curled hair and beard, he would seem to be a man come from somewhere west of the Congling Mountains. Until now he has been patiently flourishing a red-handled shubi to drive off the horseflies and flies that would settle upon the naked man, but he appears at last to have tired a little, and now he has come over beside the unglazed earthen jar and squats there with an air of importance, in the attitude of a turkey.
curious.ja: もう一人は、黄色い法衣を着て、耳に小さな青銅の環をさげた、一見、象貌の奇古な沙門である。皮膚の色が並はづれて黒い上に、髪や鬚の縮れてゐる所を見ると、どうも葱嶺の西からでも来た人間らしい。これはさつきから根気よく、朱柄の麈尾をふりふり、裸の男にたからうとする虻や蠅を追つてゐたが、流石に少しくたびれたと見えて、今では、例の素焼の瓶の側へ来て、七面鳥のやうな恰好をしながら、勿体らしくしやがんでゐる。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: The Congling are the Pamirs, the 'Onion Ranges' of Central Asia; the name marks the monk as coming from far to the west of China.
A shubi is a horsehair fly-whisk, carried by monks and men of letters to wave away insects.

curious.en: The last stands far apart from these two, under the eaves of a thatched hut in the corner of the threshing-floor. This man sports only a token beard, like a rat's tail, on the tip of his chin, and wears a black cloth gown long enough to hide his heels, with a tea-brown sash whose knot hangs sloppily. To judge from the manner in which from time to time he handles a fan made of white birds' feathers with great care, he is most likely a Confucian scholar or something of the kind.
curious.ja: あとの一人は、この二人からずつと離れて、打麦場の隅にある草房の軒下に立つてゐる。この男は、頤の先に、鼠の尻尾のやうな髯を、申訳だけに生やして、踵が隠れる程長い皁布衫に、結目をだらしなく垂らした茶褐帯と云ふ拵へである。白い鳥の羽で製つた団扇を、時々大事さうに使つてゐる容子では、多分、儒者か何かにちがひない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: All three, as if by agreement, keep their mouths shut. What is more, they hardly so much as move, as though they took extraordinary interest in something now about to happen, and for that reason were all holding their breath.
curious.ja: この三人が三人とも、云ひ合せたやうに、口を噤んでゐる。その上、碌に身動きさへもしない、何か、これから起らうとする事に、非常な興味でも持つてゐて、その為に、皆、息をひそめてゐるのではないかと思はれる。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: It must be just noon. Whether because even the dogs are taking their midday nap, not a single bark is heard. The hemp and millet that enclose the threshing-floor shine their green leaves in the sun and rest hushed and utterly still. And the sky seen beyond them, stifling with heat over its whole face, trails heat-haze, so that even the piled clouds seem to be panting in this dry spell. Look where one will, the only things that seem to breathe are these three men. And those three keep silence like the clay images enshrined in a Guandi temple....
curious.ja: 日は正に、亭午であらう。犬も午睡をしてゐるせいか、吠える声一つ聞えない。打麦場を囲んでゐる麻や黍も、青い葉を日に光らせて、ひつそりかんと静まつてゐる。それから、その末に見える空も、一面に、熱くるしく、炎靄をたゞよはせて、雲の峰さへもこの旱に、肩息をついてゐるのかと、疑はれる。見渡した所、息が通つてゐるらしいのは、この三人の男の外にない。さうして、その三人が又、関帝廟に安置してある、泥塑の像のやうに沈黙を守つてゐる。……
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: Guandi is the deified general Guan Yu, worshipped in temples filled with life-size clay figures; the point is stock-still silence.
notes.span: like the clay images enshrined in a Guandi temple

curious.en: Of course, this is no tale of Japan. — It is what happened one summer on the threshing-floor of a Liu at a place called Changshan in China.
curious.ja: 勿論、日本の話ではない。――支那の長山と云ふ所にある劉氏の打麦場で、或年の夏、起つた出来事である。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: II
curious.ja: 二
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The man lying naked in the blazing sun is the master of this threshing-floor, surnamed Liu, named Dacheng, one of the leading rich men of Changshan. This man's sole diversion is the drinking of wine, and from morning he has scarcely ever been known to part from the cup. And that, as the phrase has it, "Each time he drinks alone, he empties a whole jar" — a measure of wine beyond the common run of men. Though, as said before, "Fields by the walls, three hundred mu, half sown with millet," so there is not the least fear that his drinking should encumber his estate.
curious.ja: 裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるのは、この打麦場の主人で、姓は劉、名は大成と云ふ、長山では、屈指の素封家の一人である。この男の道楽は、酒を飲む一方で、朝から、殆、盃を離したと云ふ事がない。それも、「独酌する毎に輒、一甕を尽す」と云ふのだから、人並をはづれた酒量である。尤も前にも云つたやうに、「負郭の田三百畝、半は黍を種う」と云ふので、飲の為に家産が累はされるやうな惧は、万々ない。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: A mu is a Chinese measure of land, a fraction of an acre that varied by time and place; three hundred mu means a large estate.

curious.en: Why it is that he lies naked in the blazing sun has a history behind it, and it is this. — That day Liu was together with Sun Sensei, his companion in drinking (this is the scholar who held the white-feather fan), in a well-aired room, leaning against a bamboo-wife bolster and playing out a game on the board, when the maidservant, a yahuan, came and said, "A monk who says he is staying at the Hodoji temple or somewhere has just come, and says he must by all means see the master. What shall I do?"
curious.ja: それが、何故、裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるかと云ふと、それには、かう云ふ因縁がある。――その日、劉が、同じ飲仲間の孫先生と一しよに（これが、白羽扇を持つてゐた儒者である。）風通しのいゝ室で、竹婦人に靠れながら、棋局を闘はせてゐると、召使ひの丫鬟が来て、「唯今、宝幢寺とかにゐると云ふ、坊さんが御見えになりまして、是非、御主人に御目にかゝりたいと申しますが、いかゞ致しませう。」と云ふ。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: Hodoji follows the Japanese pronunciation of the temple's characters; in Chinese the same characters would sound quite different.
notes.span: at the Hodoji temple or somewhere

curious.en: "What, the Hodoji?" So saying, Liu blinked his small eyes as if dazzled, then, raising his fat body that looked hot in itself, ordered, "Then show him in here." Then, with a glance at Sun Sensei's face, he added, "It will be that monk, I suppose."
curious.ja: 「なに、宝幢寺？」かう云つて、劉は小さな眼を、まぶしさうに、しばたたいたが、やがて、暑さうに肥つた体を起しながら、「では、こゝへ御通し申せ。」と云ひつけた。それから、孫先生の顔をちよいと見て「大方あの坊主でせう。」とつけ加へた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The monk at the Hodoji temple is a barbarian monk come from the Western Regions. Since he both lends a hand at healing and practises the arts of the bedchamber, his fame stands high in these parts. Rumours all but miraculous are rife — that Zhang San's black cataract suddenly turned toward recovery, that Li Si's eunuch-like illness was healed on the spot, and the like. — Both men had heard these rumours. What business could have brought that barbarian monk now, taking the trouble to come all the way to Liu's? Liu, for his part, had no recollection whatever of having sent to fetch him.
curious.ja: 宝幢寺にゐる坊主と云ふのは、西域から来た蛮僧である。これが、医療も加へれば、房術も施すと云ふので、この界隈では、評判が高い。たとへば、張三の黒内障が、忽、快方に向つたとか、李四の病閹が、即座に平癒したとか、殆、奇蹟に近い噂が盛に行はれてゐるのである。――この噂は、二人とも聞いてゐた。その蛮僧が、今、何の用で、わざわざ、劉の所へ出むいて来たのであらう。勿論、劉の方から、迎へにやつた覚えなどは、全然ない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: To note it in passing, Liu was not at all a man who delighted in visitors. But when he already had one visitor with him, and a new visitor came, he would generally receive him gladly. He had a childish vanity of the sort that might be described as showing off the fact of having a visitor before a visitor. Besides, today's barbarian monk was at this time the talk everywhere. He was by no means a visitor one would be ashamed to meet. — Liu's motives in saying he would meet him lay roughly here.
curious.ja: 序に云つて置くが、劉は、一体、来客を悦ぶやうな男ではない。が、他に一人、来客がある場合に、新来の客が来たとなると、大抵ならば、快く会つてやる。客の手前、客のあるのを自慢するとでも云つたらよささうな、小供らしい虚栄心を持つてゐるからである。それに、今日の蛮僧は、この頃、どこででも評判になつてゐる。決して、会つて恥しいやうな客ではない。――劉が会はうと云ひ出した動機は、大体こんな所にあつたのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "What business can he have?"
curious.ja: 「何の用でせう。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Alms-seeking, most likely. He will be asking for some charity, I suppose."
curious.ja: 「まづ、物貰ひですな。信施でもしてくれと云ふのでせう。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: While the two were talking such things over between them, presently there entered, guided in by the yahuan, a monk of strange aspect, tall and with eyes like cut violet quartz. He wore a yellow robe, his grown-out curling hair hanging tiresomely over his shoulders. Still holding his red-handled shubi, he planted himself heavily in the middle of the room. He offered no greeting, nor did he speak.
curious.ja: こんな事を、二人で話してゐる内に、やがて、丫鬟の案内で、はいつて来たのを見ると、背の高い、紫石稜のやうな眼をした、異形な沙門である。黄色い法衣を着て、その肩に、縮れた髪の伸びたのを、うるささうに垂らしてゐる。それが、朱柄の麈尾を持つたまゝ、のつそり室のまん中に立つた。挨拶もしなければ、口もきかない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Liu hesitated for a while, but as that somehow grew unsettling to him, he ventured, "Have you some business with me?"
curious.ja: 劉は、しばらく、ためらつてゐたが、その内に、それが何となく、不安になつて来たので「何か御用かな。」と訊いて見た。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Whereupon the barbarian monk said, "You are the one, I take it, who is fond of wine."
curious.ja: すると、蛮僧が云つた。「あなたでせうな、酒が好きなのは。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "I am." The question was so abrupt that Liu, as he gave his vague answer, looked toward Sun Sensei as if seeking rescue. Sun Sensei, with a composed air, went on laying stones on the board by himself. He showed no disposition to take any part.
curious.ja: 「さやう。」劉は、あまり問が唐突なので、曖昧な返事をしながら、救を求めるやうに、孫先生の方を見た。孫先生は、すまして、独りで、盤面に石を下してゐる。まるで、取り合ふ容子はない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "You are afflicted with a rare disease. Are you aware of it?" the barbarian monk said, as if to make sure. Liu, hearing of a disease, made a dubious face, and, stroking his bamboo wife,
curious.ja: 「あなたは、珍しい病に罹つて御出になる。それを御存知ですかな。」蛮僧は念を押すやうに、かう云つた。劉は、病と聞いたので、けげんな顔をして、竹婦人を撫でながら、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "A disease — you say?"
curious.ja: 「病――ですかな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It is."
curious.ja: 「さうです。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, since I was a child..." As Liu was about to say something more, the barbarian monk cut him off.
curious.ja: 「いや、幼少の時から……」劉が何か云はうとすると、蛮僧はそれを遮つて、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "However much wine you drink, you never get drunk."
curious.ja: 「酒を飲まれても、酔ひますまいな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "..." Liu stared at the man's face and shut his mouth. In fact, however much wine this man drank, he had never once been drunk.
curious.ja: 「……」劉は、ぢろぢろ、相手の顔を見ながら、口を噤んでしまつた。実際この男は、いくら酒を飲んでも、酔つた事がないのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That is the proof of the disease," the barbarian monk went on with a faint smile. "There is a wine worm in your belly. Unless it is removed, this disease will not be cured. This poor monk has come to cure your disease."
curious.ja: 「それが、病の証拠ですよ。」蛮僧は、うす笑をしながら、語をついで、「腹中に酒虫がゐる。それを除かないと、この病は癒りません。貧道は、あなたの病を癒しに来たのです。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Can it be cured?" Liu cried out before he knew it, in an uncertain voice. And he was ashamed of himself for it.
curious.ja: 「癒りますかな。」劉は思はず覚束なさうな声を出した。さうして、自分でそれを恥ぢた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It can be cured, which is why I have come."
curious.ja: 「癒ればこそ、来ましたが。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Then Sun Sensei, who had till now listened in silence to the exchange of questions and answers, suddenly put in a word.
curious.ja: すると、今まで、黙つて、問答を聞いてゐた孫先生が、急に語を挟んだ。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Will you use some medicine?"
curious.ja: 「何か、薬でも御用ひか。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, there is no need to use medicine or the like," the barbarian monk answered ungraciously.
curious.ja: 「いや、薬なぞは用ひるまでもありません。」蛮僧は不愛想に、かう答へた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Sun Sensei by nature despised the two teachings of the Daoists and the Buddhists almost without reason. Hence he had rarely ever spoken a word when in company with a Daoist priest or a Buddhist monk. That he had now taken a sudden fancy to intervene was wholly because his interest had been stirred by the words wine worm, for Sensei, who loved wine, hearing this, had grown a little uneasy lest there be a wine worm in his own belly as well. On hearing the barbarian monk's grudging answer, however, he suddenly felt as if he himself had been made a fool of, so with a slight grimace he began once more in silence to lay the pieces down as before. And at the same time he thought inwardly how foolish of his host Liu to receive such an arrogant monk.
curious.ja: 孫先生は、元来、道仏の二教を殆、無理由に軽蔑してゐる。だから、道士とか僧侶とかと一しよになつても、口をきいた事は滅多にない。それが、今ふと口を出す気になつたのは、全く酒虫と云ふ語の興味に動かされたからで、酒の好きな先生は、これを聞くと、自分の腹の中にも、酒虫がゐはしないかと、聊、不安になつて来たのである。所が、蛮僧の不承不承な答を聞くと、急に、自分が莫迦にされたやうな気がしたので、先生はちよいと顔をしかめながら、又元の通り、黙々として棋子を下しはじめた。さうして、それと同時に、内心、こんな横柄な坊主に会つたり何ぞする主人の劉を、莫迦げてゐると思ひ出した。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Liu, for his part, of course paid no heed to any of this.
curious.ja: 劉の方では、勿論そんな事には頓着しない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Then will you use needles?"
curious.ja: 「では、針でも使ひますかな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, it is a thing of still less trouble."
curious.ja: 「なに、もつと造作のない事です。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Then is it a spell?"
curious.ja: 「では呪ですかな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, nor is it a spell."
curious.ja: 「いや、呪でもありません。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: After repeating such talk, the barbarian monk briefly explained the cure to them. — By his account, one had only to strip naked and keep still in the sun. To Liu this seemed a very easy matter. If so small a thing would cure him, there was nothing better than to be cured. And, though he was not aware of it, he was also a little moved by curiosity at undergoing the barbarian monk's treatment.
curious.ja: かう云ふ会話を繰返した末に、蛮僧は、簡単に、その療法を説明して聞かせた。――それによるに、唯、裸になつて、日向にぢつとしてゐさへすればよいと云ふのである。劉には、それが、甚、容易な事のやうに思はれた。その位の事で癒るなら、癒して貰ふのに越した事はない。その上、意識してはゐなかつたが、蛮僧の治療を受けると云ふ点で、好奇心も少しは動いてゐた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: So at last Liu bowed his head of his own accord, and it came to this: "Then I must ask you to cure me, if you please." — Such is the reason why Liu lies naked upon the threshing-floor in the blazing sun.
curious.ja: そこでとうとう、劉も、こつちから頭を下げて、「では、どうか一つ、癒して頂きませう。」と云ふ事になつた。――劉が、裸で、炎天の打麦場にねころんでゐるのには、かう云ふ謂れが、あるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Thereupon, saying he must not stir, the barbarian monk wound Liu's body round and round with thin cord. Then, bidding one of the servants, he had an unglazed earthen jar with wine in it brought to Liu's pillow. That Sun Sensei, the good friend of the wine-mound, should in the course of things have come to stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
curious.ja: すると蛮僧は、身動きをしてはいけないと云ふので、劉の体を細引で、ぐるぐる巻にした。それから、僮僕の一人に云ひつけて、酒を入れた素焼の瓶を一つ、劉の枕もとへ持つて来させた。当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: A Chinese literary phrase for a devoted drinking companion, picturing wine as a hill to lie upon.
notes.span: the good friend of the wine-mound

curious.en: What sort of thing the wine worm is, what happens when it is no longer in the belly, and what the jar of wine at the pillow is for, no one knows but the barbarian monk alone. To put it so, Liu, who has gone out naked into the blazing sun knowing nothing, may seem very heedless, but what ordinary men do when they receive schooling and the like is in truth for the most part the same sort of thing.
curious.ja: 酒虫と云ふ物が、どんな物だか、それが腹の中にゐなくなると、どうなるのだか、枕もとにある酒の瓶は、何にするつもりなのだか、それを知つてゐるのは、蛮僧の外に一人もない。かう云ふと、何も知らずに、炎天へ裸で出てゐる劉は、甚、迂濶なやうに思はれるが、普通の人間が、学校の教育などをうけるのも、実は大抵、これと同じやうな事をしてゐるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: III
curious.ja: 三
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: It is hot. Sweat comes welling up with a prickle across the brow, and when it seems to have beaded it comes trickling, lukewarm, toward the eyes. As ill luck will have it, he is bound with thin cord, so of course there is no putting out a hand to wipe it. He tries moving his neck to turn the course of the sweat aside, but at that instant a violent dizziness seems ready to come on, so to his disappointment he gave up this plan too. All the while the sweat without ceremony wets the eyelids and, passing from the side of the nose round the mouth, runs on down beneath the chin. It is disagreeable beyond measure.
curious.ja: 暑い。額へ汗がぢりぢりと湧いて来て、それが玉になつたかと思ふと、つうつと生暖く、眼の方へ流れて来る。生憎、細引でしばられてゐるから、手を出して拭ふ訳には、勿論行かない。そこで、首を動かして、汗の進路を変へやうとすると、その途端に、はげしく眩暈がしさうな気がしたので、残念ながら、この計画も亦、見合せる事にした。その中に、汗は遠慮なく、眶をぬらして、鼻の側から口許をまはりながら、頤の下まで流れて行く。気味が悪い事夥しい。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Until then he had lain with eyes open, staring hard at the sky seared white and the hemp-field with its drooping leaves, but once the sweat began to pour without restraint even that had to be given up. It was then that Liu learned for the first time that sweat stings when it gets into the eyes. And so, with the face of a sheep in the slaughterhouse, meekly shutting his eyes and lying still while the sun beats down upon him, now in turn the skin of the upper parts, face or body alike, began gradually to feel a certain pain. Across every inch of skin something tugs in every direction at once, and the skin has no give in it at all. A pain that might best be described as a tingling everywhere. This is not the misery of prickly heat. Liu began to find it hateful that he had taken the barbarian monk's cure.
curious.ja: それまでは、眼を開いて、白く焦された空や、葉をたらした麻畑を、まじ〳〵と眺めてゐたが、汗が無暗に流れるやうになつてからは、それさへ断念しなければならなくなつた。劉は、この時、始めて、汗が眼にはいると、しみるものだと云ふ事を、知つたのである。そこで、屠所の羊の様な顔をして、神妙に眼をつぶりながら、ぢつと日に照りつけられてゐると、今度は、顔と云はず体と云はず、上になつてゐる部分の皮膚が、次第に或痛みを感じるやうになつて来た。皮膚の全面に、あらゆる方向へ動かうとする力が働いてゐるが、皮膚自身は、それに対して、毫も弾力を持つてゐない。それでどこもかしこも、ぴり〳〵する――とでも説明したら、よからうと思ふ痛みである。これは、汗所の苦しさではない。劉は、少し蛮僧の治療をうけたのが、忌々しくなつて来た。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: However, thinking it over afterwards, this was still the part that was less painful. — Before long his throat grows parched. Liu too knows the story of how Cao Mengde, or someone, cured the thirst of his soldiers by telling them there was a plum grove ahead. But now, picture as he will the sweet sourness of plums in his mind, his thirst is not a whit the less for it. He moves his jaw about, he bites his tongue, yet inside his mouth still keeps its heat. That too might still have been somewhat easier to bear, had there not been the unglazed earthen jar at his pillow. From the mouth of the jar the rich fragrant smell of wine comes without break to assail his nose. And, though it may be fancy, he even feels that smell growing stronger with every minute. Thinking at least to look at the jar, Liu opened his eyes. Glancing upward, he sees the mouth of the jar and something like half of its amply bulging body. That alone is what he sees, but at the same time there rises before Liu's imagination the sight of wine the colour of gold brimming in the dim interior of that jar. Before he knew it he had licked his cracked lips with his dry tongue, yet there is no sign at all of saliva springing. Even the sweat, dried now by the sun, no longer flows as before.
curious.ja: しかし、これは、後になつて考へて見ると、まだ苦しくない方の部だつたのである。――そのうちに、喉が渇いて来た。劉も、曹孟徳か誰かが、前路に梅林ありと云つて、軍士の渇を医したと云ふ事は知つてゐる。が、今の場合、いくら、梅子の甘酸を念頭に浮べて見ても、喉の渇く事は、少しも前と変りがない。頤を動かして見たり、舌を噛んで見たりしたが、口の中は依然として熱を持つてゐる。それも、枕もとの素焼の瓶がなかつたら、まだ幾分でも、我慢がし易かつたのに違ひない。所が、瓶の口からは、芬々たる酒香が、間断なく、劉の鼻を襲つて来る。しかも、気のせいか、その酒香が、一分毎に、益々高くなつて来るやうな心もちさへする。劉は、せめて、瓶だけでも見ようと思つて、眼をあけた。上眼を使つて見ると、瓶の口と、応揚にふくれた胴の半分ばかりが、眼にはいる。眼にはいるのは、それだけであるが、同時に、劉の想像には、その瓶のうす暗い内部に、黄金のやうな色をした酒のなみ〳〵と湛へてゐる容子が、浮んで来た。思はず、ひびの出来た唇を、乾いた舌で舐めまはして見たが、唾の湧く気色は、更にない。汗さへ今では、日に干されて、前のやうには、流れなくなつてしまつた。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: Cao Mengde is Cao Cao (155-220), whose soldiers, thirsty on the march, are said to have been revived by hearing of plums ahead and watering at the mouth.
notes.span: telling them there was a plum grove ahead

curious.en: Then a violent dizziness came, two or three times in succession. The headache has not abated since some time ago. In his heart Liu thought the barbarian monk ever more hateful. And he thought too why a man of his standing should have let such a fellow talk him round into suffering so foolish a torment. Meanwhile his throat grows ever more parched. His chest turns strangely queasy. He can no longer bear it, to lie still. So at last Liu resolved, and, panting, opened his mouth, meaning to ask the barbarian monk at his pillow to call off the cure. —
curious.ja: すると、はげしい眩暈が、つづいて、二三度起つた。頭痛はさつきから、しつきりなしにしてゐる。劉は、心の中で愈、蛮僧を怨めしく思つた。それから又何故、自分ともあるものが、あんな人間の口車に乗つて、こんな莫迦げた苦しみをするのだらうとも思つた。そのうちに、喉は、益々、渇いて来る。胸は妙にむかついて来る。もう我慢にも、ぢつとしてはゐられない。そこで劉はとう〳〵思切つて、枕もとの蛮僧に、療治の中止を申込むつもりで、喘ぎながら、口を開いた。――
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: At that very instant. Liu began to feel an indescribable lump creeping little by little from his chest up toward his throat. At one moment it seems to writhe like an earthworm, at another to edge along little by little like a gecko. In any case some soft thing, soft as it is, comes wriggling and pressing up the gullet. And at last, when it has forced its way past beneath the Adam's apple, all at once it slips slick out of the dark place like a loach or something and flies outward with force.
curious.ja: すると、その途端である。劉は、何とも知れない塊が、少しづゝ胸から喉へ這ひ上つて来るのを感じ出した。それが或は蚯蚓のやうに、蠕動してゐるかと思ふと、或は守宮のやうに、少しづゝ居ざつてゐるやうでもある。兎に角或柔い物が、柔いなりに、むづりむづりと、食道を上へせり上つて来るのである。さうしてとうとうしまひに、それが、喉仏の下を、無理にすりぬけたと思ふと、今度はいきなり、鰌か何かのやうにぬるりと暗い所をぬけ出して、勢よく外へとんで出た。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: And with that, from the quarter of the familiar unglazed earthen jar, there sounded a plop, as of something falling into wine.
curious.ja: と、その拍子に、例の素焼の瓶の方で、ぽちやりと、何か酒の中へ落ちるやうな音がした。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Upon this the barbarian monk suddenly heaved himself up from where he had settled and began to undo the thin cord wound about Liu's body. The wine worm is out, so be at ease, is what he means.
curious.ja: すると、蛮僧が、急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて、劉の体にかゝつてゐる、細引を解きはじめた。もう、酒虫が出たから、安心しろと云ふのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Has it come out?" Liu said as if groaning, lifting his swimming head, and out of sheer curiosity, forgetting even his thirst, crawled naked to the side of the jar. At this, Sun Sensei too, shading himself from the sun with his white-feather fan, came hurrying toward the two. When all three together peered into the jar, a thing like a small salamander, flesh-coloured as red clay, was swimming in the wine. In length perhaps three sun. It had a mouth, and it had eyes. As it swam it seemed somehow to be drinking the wine. At the sight of it Liu felt suddenly sick. ...
curious.ja: 「出ましたかな。」劉は、呻くやうにかう云つて、ふらふらする頭を起しながら、物珍しさの余り、喉の渇いたのも忘れて、裸のまま、瓶の側へ這ひよつた。それと見ると、孫先生も、白羽扇で日をよけながら、急いで、二人の方へやつて来る。さて、三人揃つて瓶の中を覗きこむと、肉の色が朱泥に似た、小さな山椒魚のやうなものが、酒の中を泳いでゐる。長さは、三寸ばかりであらう。口もあれば、眼もある。どうやら、泳ぎながら、酒を飲んでゐるらしい。劉はこれを見ると、急に胸が悪くなつた。……
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: A sun is a little over three centimetres, so about nine centimetres in all.

curious.en: IV
curious.ja: 四
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The effect of the barbarian monk's treatment appeared at once. From that day Liu Dacheng abruptly could drink no more wine. Now he will not bear even to smell it, they say. Strangely, from that time Liu's health began to fail little by little. This year is three years since he spat out the wine worm, and no trace remains of the round, fat figure of former years. Skin of poor lustre, greasy still, wraps the harsh bones of his face, and frost-touched hair at the temples survives only faintly, and in a year none knows how many times he takes to his bed, they say.
curious.ja: 蛮僧の治療の効は、覿面に現れた。劉大成は、その日から、ぱつたり酒が飲めなくなつたのである。今は、匂を嗅ぐのも、嫌だと云ふ。所が、不思議な事に、劉の健康が、それから、少しづつ、衰へて来た。今年で、酒虫を吐いてから、三年になるが、往年の丸丸と肥つてゐた俤は、何処にもない。色光沢の悪い皮膚が、脂じみたまま、険しい顔の骨を包んで、霜に侵された双髩が、纔に、顳顬の上に、残つてゐるばかり、一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位ださうである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Yet it was not Liu's health alone that has failed since then. His estate too has declined headlong, and now of the fields by the walls counted as three hundred mu, most have passed into other hands. Liu himself, perforce, has taken the plough in unpractised hands and passes his days, day by day, in cheerlessness.
curious.ja: しかし、それ以来、衰へたのは、劉の健康ばかりではない。劉の家産も亦とんとん拍子に傾いて、今では、三百畝を以て数へた負郭の田も、多くは人の手に渡つた。劉自身も、余儀なく、馴れない手に鋤を執つて、佗しいその日その日を送つてゐるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Since spitting out the wine worm, why has Liu's health failed? Why has the estate declined — once you set the spitting-out of the wine worm side by side with Liu's later ruin as cause and effect, it is a question anyone would ask. In fact this question has been repeated by people of every occupation living in Changshan, and from the mouths of those people answers of every kind have been given. The three answers set down here are in truth no more than the most representative chosen from among them.
curious.ja: 酒虫を吐いて以来、何故、劉の健康が衰へたか。何故、家産が傾いたか――酒虫を吐いたと云ふ事と、劉のその後の零落とを、因果の関係に並べて見る以上、これは、誰にでも起りやすい疑問である。現にこの疑問は、長山に住んでゐる、あらゆる職業の人人によつて繰返され、且、それらの人人の口から、あらゆる種類の答を与へられた。今、ここに挙げる三つの答も、実はその中から、最、代表的なものを選んだのに過ぎない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: First answer. The wine worm was Liu's fortune, and not Liu's disease. Through chancing to meet with a benighted barbarian monk, he willingly came to lose this heaven-given fortune.
curious.ja: 第一の答。酒虫は、劉の福であつて、劉の病ではない。偶、暗愚の蛮僧に遇つた為に、好んで、この天与の福を失ふやうな事になつたのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Second answer. The wine worm was Liu's disease, and not Liu's fortune. For to drain a whole jar at a single drinking is quite beyond what an ordinary man can conceive. Had the wine worm not been removed, Liu must soon have died, without doubt. That being so, poverty and sickness arriving each in turn should rather be called happiness for Liu.
curious.ja: 第二の答。酒虫は、劉の病であつて、劉の福ではない。何故と云へば、一飲一甕を尽すなどと云ふ事は、到底、常人の考へられない所だからである。そこで、もし酒虫を除かなかつたなら、劉は必久しからずして、死んだのに相違ない。して見ると、貧病、迭に至るのも、寧劉にとつては、幸福と云ふべきである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Third answer. The wine worm was neither Liu's disease nor Liu's fortune. Liu from of old drank nothing but wine. If wine is taken from Liu's life, afterwards nothing remains. That being so, Liu is the wine worm, the wine worm is Liu. Therefore Liu's parting with the wine worm is the same as killing himself. In short, from the day he could drink wine no more, Liu is Liu and yet is not Liu. If Liu himself was already gone, that the health and estate of the Liu of former days should have been lost would be only natural.
curious.ja: 第三の答。酒虫は、劉の病でもなければ、劉の福でもない。劉は、昔から酒ばかり飲んでゐた。劉の一生から酒を除けば、後には、何も残らない。して見ると、劉は即酒虫、酒虫は即劉である。だから、劉が酒虫を去つたのは自ら己を殺したのも同前である。つまり、酒が飲めなくなつた日から、劉は劉にして、劉ではない。劉自身が既になくなつてゐたとしたら、昔日の劉の健康なり家産なりが、失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Which of these answers comes nearest to the mark, I myself do not know. I have merely listed such moral judgments at the end of this tale, in imitation of the *Didacticism* of Chinese novelists.
curious.ja: これらの答の中で、どれが、最よく、当を得てゐるか、それは自分にもわからない。自分は、唯、支那の小説家の Didacticism に倣つて、かう云ふ道徳的な判断を、この話の最後に、列挙して見たまでゝある。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: The English word is printed with a capital D in the Japanese, part of the narrator's pose as an imitator of Chinese storytellers who close with morals.

curious.en: — Fourth Month of the Fifth Year —
curious.ja: ――五年四月――
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: The tale signs off with a month and a year-number only, without an era name to fix which fifth year is meant.
notes.span: Fourth Month of the Fifth Year

student.en: I
student.ja: 一
student.label: house-checked

student.en: It is a heat unknown in recent years. Wherever one looks, the roof-tiles of the mud-plastered houses reflect the sunlight dully, like lead, so that even the swallows' nests hung beneath them seem, at this rate, like to steam the chicks and eggs within to death just as they are. What is more, every field, hemp or millet, hangs its head limply in the heat rising from the earth, and there is not one thing that, for all its greenness, is not wilted. The sky seen above those fields, too, whether from the warm vapours of these last days, the air near the ground, though clear, hangs thick and turbid, and here and there the piled clouds, like hail parched in an earthen pan, mere shapes, float in clumps. — The tale of the "wine worm" begins with three men who in this weather have gone out of their way to be upon a threshing-floor in the blazing sun.
student.ja: 近年にない暑さである。どこを見ても、泥で固めた家々の屋根瓦が、鉛のやうに鈍く日の光を反射して、その下に懸けてある燕の巣さへ、この塩梅では中にゐる雛や卵を、そのまゝ蒸殺してしまふかと思はれる。まして、畑と云ふ畑は、麻でも黍でも、皆、土いきれにぐつたりと頭をさげて、何一つ、青いなりに、萎れてゐないものはない。その畑の上に見える空も、この頃の温気に中てられたせいか、地上に近い大気は、晴れながら、どんよりと濁つて、その所々に、霰を炮烙で煎つたやうな、形ばかりの雲の峰が、つぶつぶと浮かんでゐる。――「酒虫」の話は、この陽気に、わざ〳〵炎天の打麦場へ出てゐる、三人の男で始まるのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Strangely, one of them lies stark naked on his back on the bare ground. What is more, for some reason or other, hand and foot he is wound round and round with thin cord. Yet the man himself shows no sign of suffering it as a hardship. He is short, of good colour, somehow giving a sense of dull heaviness, a man fat as a pig. Then a handy-sized unglazed earthen jar is set at this man's pillow, but what is inside that, too, is not known.
student.ja: 不思議な事に、その中の一人は、素裸で、仰向けに地面へ寝ころんでゐる。おまけに、どう云ふ訳だか、細引で、手も足もぐる〳〵巻にされてゐる。が格別当人は、それを苦に病んでゐる容子もない。背の低い、血色の好い、どことなく鈍重と云ふ感じを起させる、豚のやうに肥つた男である。それから手ごろな素焼の瓶が一つ、この男の枕もとに置いてあるが、これも中に何がはいつてゐるのだか、わからない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Another is a monk of strikingly antique aspect, in a yellow robe with a small bronze ring hung from his ear. His skin is remarkably black in colour, and to judge from his curled hair and beard, he would seem to be a man come from somewhere west of the Congling Mountains. Until now he has been patiently flourishing a red-handled shubi to drive off the horseflies and flies that would settle upon the naked man, but he appears at last to have tired a little, and now he has come over beside the unglazed earthen jar and squats there with an air of importance, in the attitude of a turkey.
student.ja: もう一人は、黄色い法衣を着て、耳に小さな青銅の環をさげた、一見、象貌の奇古な沙門である。皮膚の色が並はづれて黒い上に、髪や鬚の縮れてゐる所を見ると、どうも葱嶺の西からでも来た人間らしい。これはさつきから根気よく、朱柄の麈尾をふりふり、裸の男にたからうとする虻や蠅を追つてゐたが、流石に少しくたびれたと見えて、今では、例の素焼の瓶の側へ来て、七面鳥のやうな恰好をしながら、勿体らしくしやがんでゐる。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The last stands far apart from these two, under the eaves of a thatched hut in the corner of the threshing-floor. This man sports only a token beard, like a rat's tail, on the tip of his chin, and wears a black cloth gown long enough to hide his heels, with a tea-brown sash whose knot hangs sloppily. To judge from the manner in which from time to time he handles a fan made of white birds' feathers with great care, he is most likely a Confucian scholar or something of the kind.
student.ja: あとの一人は、この二人からずつと離れて、打麦場の隅にある草房の軒下に立つてゐる。この男は、頤の先に、鼠の尻尾のやうな髯を、申訳だけに生やして、踵が隠れる程長い皁布衫に、結目をだらしなく垂らした茶褐帯と云ふ拵へである。白い鳥の羽で製つた団扇を、時々大事さうに使つてゐる容子では、多分、儒者か何かにちがひない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: All three, as if by agreement, keep their mouths shut. What is more, they hardly so much as move, as though they took extraordinary interest in something now about to happen, and for that reason were all holding their breath.
student.ja: この三人が三人とも、云ひ合せたやうに、口を噤んでゐる。その上、碌に身動きさへもしない、何か、これから起らうとする事に、非常な興味でも持つてゐて、その為に、皆、息をひそめてゐるのではないかと思はれる。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: It must be just noon. Whether because even the dogs are taking their midday nap, not a single bark is heard. The hemp and millet that enclose the threshing-floor shine their green leaves in the sun and rest hushed and utterly still. And the sky seen beyond them, stifling with heat over its whole face, trails heat-haze, so that even the piled clouds seem to be panting in this dry spell. Look where one will, the only things that seem to breathe are these three men. And those three keep silence like the clay images enshrined in a Guandi temple....
student.ja: 日は正に、亭午であらう。犬も午睡をしてゐるせいか、吠える声一つ聞えない。打麦場を囲んでゐる麻や黍も、青い葉を日に光らせて、ひつそりかんと静まつてゐる。それから、その末に見える空も、一面に、熱くるしく、炎靄をたゞよはせて、雲の峰さへもこの旱に、肩息をついてゐるのかと、疑はれる。見渡した所、息が通つてゐるらしいのは、この三人の男の外にない。さうして、その三人が又、関帝廟に安置してある、泥塑の像のやうに沈黙を守つてゐる。……
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Of course, this is no tale of Japan. — It is what happened one summer on the threshing-floor of a Liu at a place called Changshan in China.
student.ja: 勿論、日本の話ではない。――支那の長山と云ふ所にある劉氏の打麦場で、或年の夏、起つた出来事である。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: II
student.ja: 二
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The man lying naked in the blazing sun is the master of this threshing-floor, surnamed Liu, named Dacheng, one of the leading rich men of Changshan. This man's sole diversion is the drinking of wine, and from morning he has scarcely ever been known to part from the cup. And that, as the phrase has it, "Each time he drinks alone, he empties a whole jar" — a measure of wine beyond the common run of men. Though, as said before, "Fields by the walls, three hundred mu, half sown with millet," so there is not the least fear that his drinking should encumber his estate.
student.ja: 裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるのは、この打麦場の主人で、姓は劉、名は大成と云ふ、長山では、屈指の素封家の一人である。この男の道楽は、酒を飲む一方で、朝から、殆、盃を離したと云ふ事がない。それも、「独酌する毎に輒、一甕を尽す」と云ふのだから、人並をはづれた酒量である。尤も前にも云つたやうに、「負郭の田三百畝、半は黍を種う」と云ふので、飲の為に家産が累はされるやうな惧は、万々ない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Why it is that he lies naked in the blazing sun has a history behind it, and it is this. — That day Liu was together with Sun Sensei, his companion in drinking (this is the scholar who held the white-feather fan), in a well-aired room, leaning against a bamboo-wife bolster and playing out a game on the board, when the maidservant, a yahuan, came and said, "A monk who says he is staying at the Hodoji temple or somewhere has just come, and says he must by all means see the master. What shall I do?"
student.ja: それが、何故、裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるかと云ふと、それには、かう云ふ因縁がある。――その日、劉が、同じ飲仲間の孫先生と一しよに（これが、白羽扇を持つてゐた儒者である。）風通しのいゝ室で、竹婦人に靠れながら、棋局を闘はせてゐると、召使ひの丫鬟が来て、「唯今、宝幢寺とかにゐると云ふ、坊さんが御見えになりまして、是非、御主人に御目にかゝりたいと申しますが、いかゞ致しませう。」と云ふ。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "What, the Hodoji?" So saying, Liu blinked his small eyes as if dazzled, then, raising his fat body that looked hot in itself, ordered, "Then show him in here." Then, with a glance at Sun Sensei's face, he added, "It will be that monk, I suppose."
student.ja: 「なに、宝幢寺？」かう云つて、劉は小さな眼を、まぶしさうに、しばたたいたが、やがて、暑さうに肥つた体を起しながら、「では、こゝへ御通し申せ。」と云ひつけた。それから、孫先生の顔をちよいと見て「大方あの坊主でせう。」とつけ加へた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The monk at the Hodoji temple is a barbarian monk come from the Western Regions. Since he both lends a hand at healing and practises the arts of the bedchamber, his fame stands high in these parts. Rumours all but miraculous are rife — that Zhang San's black cataract suddenly turned toward recovery, that Li Si's eunuch-like illness was healed on the spot, and the like. — Both men had heard these rumours. What business could have brought that barbarian monk now, taking the trouble to come all the way to Liu's? Liu, for his part, had no recollection whatever of having sent to fetch him.
student.ja: 宝幢寺にゐる坊主と云ふのは、西域から来た蛮僧である。これが、医療も加へれば、房術も施すと云ふので、この界隈では、評判が高い。たとへば、張三の黒内障が、忽、快方に向つたとか、李四の病閹が、即座に平癒したとか、殆、奇蹟に近い噂が盛に行はれてゐるのである。――この噂は、二人とも聞いてゐた。その蛮僧が、今、何の用で、わざわざ、劉の所へ出むいて来たのであらう。勿論、劉の方から、迎へにやつた覚えなどは、全然ない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: To note it in passing, Liu was not at all a man who delighted in visitors. But when he already had one visitor with him, and a new visitor came, he would generally receive him gladly. He had a childish vanity of the sort that might be described as showing off the fact of having a visitor before a visitor. Besides, today's barbarian monk was at this time the talk everywhere. He was by no means a visitor one would be ashamed to meet. — Liu's motives in saying he would meet him lay roughly here.
student.ja: 序に云つて置くが、劉は、一体、来客を悦ぶやうな男ではない。が、他に一人、来客がある場合に、新来の客が来たとなると、大抵ならば、快く会つてやる。客の手前、客のあるのを自慢するとでも云つたらよささうな、小供らしい虚栄心を持つてゐるからである。それに、今日の蛮僧は、この頃、どこででも評判になつてゐる。決して、会つて恥しいやうな客ではない。――劉が会はうと云ひ出した動機は、大体こんな所にあつたのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "What business can he have?"
student.ja: 「何の用でせう。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Alms-seeking, most likely. He will be asking for some charity, I suppose."
student.ja: 「まづ、物貰ひですな。信施でもしてくれと云ふのでせう。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: While the two were talking such things over between them, presently there entered, guided in by the yahuan, a monk of strange aspect, tall and with eyes like cut violet quartz. He wore a yellow robe, his grown-out curling hair hanging tiresomely over his shoulders. Still holding his red-handled shubi, he planted himself heavily in the middle of the room. He offered no greeting, nor did he speak.
student.ja: こんな事を、二人で話してゐる内に、やがて、丫鬟の案内で、はいつて来たのを見ると、背の高い、紫石稜のやうな眼をした、異形な沙門である。黄色い法衣を着て、その肩に、縮れた髪の伸びたのを、うるささうに垂らしてゐる。それが、朱柄の麈尾を持つたまゝ、のつそり室のまん中に立つた。挨拶もしなければ、口もきかない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Liu hesitated for a while, but as that somehow grew unsettling to him, he ventured, "Have you some business with me?"
student.ja: 劉は、しばらく、ためらつてゐたが、その内に、それが何となく、不安になつて来たので「何か御用かな。」と訊いて見た。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Whereupon the barbarian monk said, "You are the one, I take it, who is fond of wine."
student.ja: すると、蛮僧が云つた。「あなたでせうな、酒が好きなのは。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "I am." The question was so abrupt that Liu, as he gave his vague answer, looked toward Sun Sensei as if seeking rescue. Sun Sensei, with a composed air, went on laying stones on the board by himself. He showed no disposition to take any part.
student.ja: 「さやう。」劉は、あまり問が唐突なので、曖昧な返事をしながら、救を求めるやうに、孫先生の方を見た。孫先生は、すまして、独りで、盤面に石を下してゐる。まるで、取り合ふ容子はない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "You are afflicted with a rare disease. Are you aware of it?" the barbarian monk said, as if to make sure. Liu, hearing of a disease, made a dubious face, and, stroking his bamboo wife,
student.ja: 「あなたは、珍しい病に罹つて御出になる。それを御存知ですかな。」蛮僧は念を押すやうに、かう云つた。劉は、病と聞いたので、けげんな顔をして、竹婦人を撫でながら、
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "A disease — you say?"
student.ja: 「病――ですかな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "It is."
student.ja: 「さうです。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "No, since I was a child..." As Liu was about to say something more, the barbarian monk cut him off.
student.ja: 「いや、幼少の時から……」劉が何か云はうとすると、蛮僧はそれを遮つて、
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "However much wine you drink, you never get drunk."
student.ja: 「酒を飲まれても、酔ひますまいな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "..." Liu stared at the man's face and shut his mouth. In fact, however much wine this man drank, he had never once been drunk.
student.ja: 「……」劉は、ぢろぢろ、相手の顔を見ながら、口を噤んでしまつた。実際この男は、いくら酒を飲んでも、酔つた事がないのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That is the proof of the disease," the barbarian monk went on with a faint smile. "There is a wine worm in your belly. Unless it is removed, this disease will not be cured. This poor monk has come to cure your disease."
student.ja: 「それが、病の証拠ですよ。」蛮僧は、うす笑をしながら、語をついで、「腹中に酒虫がゐる。それを除かないと、この病は癒りません。貧道は、あなたの病を癒しに来たのです。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Can it be cured?" Liu cried out before he knew it, in an uncertain voice. And he was ashamed of himself for it.
student.ja: 「癒りますかな。」劉は思はず覚束なさうな声を出した。さうして、自分でそれを恥ぢた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "It can be cured, which is why I have come."
student.ja: 「癒ればこそ、来ましたが。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Then Sun Sensei, who had till now listened in silence to the exchange of questions and answers, suddenly put in a word.
student.ja: すると、今まで、黙つて、問答を聞いてゐた孫先生が、急に語を挟んだ。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Will you use some medicine?"
student.ja: 「何か、薬でも御用ひか。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "No, there is no need to use medicine or the like," the barbarian monk answered ungraciously.
student.ja: 「いや、薬なぞは用ひるまでもありません。」蛮僧は不愛想に、かう答へた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Sun Sensei by nature despised the two teachings of the Daoists and the Buddhists almost without reason. Hence he had rarely ever spoken a word when in company with a Daoist priest or a Buddhist monk. That he had now taken a sudden fancy to intervene was wholly because his interest had been stirred by the words wine worm, for Sensei, who loved wine, hearing this, had grown a little uneasy lest there be a wine worm in his own belly as well. On hearing the barbarian monk's grudging answer, however, he suddenly felt as if he himself had been made a fool of, so with a slight grimace he began once more in silence to lay the pieces down as before. And at the same time he thought inwardly how foolish of his host Liu to receive such an arrogant monk.
student.ja: 孫先生は、元来、道仏の二教を殆、無理由に軽蔑してゐる。だから、道士とか僧侶とかと一しよになつても、口をきいた事は滅多にない。それが、今ふと口を出す気になつたのは、全く酒虫と云ふ語の興味に動かされたからで、酒の好きな先生は、これを聞くと、自分の腹の中にも、酒虫がゐはしないかと、聊、不安になつて来たのである。所が、蛮僧の不承不承な答を聞くと、急に、自分が莫迦にされたやうな気がしたので、先生はちよいと顔をしかめながら、又元の通り、黙々として棋子を下しはじめた。さうして、それと同時に、内心、こんな横柄な坊主に会つたり何ぞする主人の劉を、莫迦げてゐると思ひ出した。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Liu, for his part, of course paid no heed to any of this.
student.ja: 劉の方では、勿論そんな事には頓着しない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Then will you use needles?"
student.ja: 「では、針でも使ひますかな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "No, it is a thing of still less trouble."
student.ja: 「なに、もつと造作のない事です。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Then is it a spell?"
student.ja: 「では呪ですかな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "No, nor is it a spell."
student.ja: 「いや、呪でもありません。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: After repeating such talk, the barbarian monk briefly explained the cure to them. — By his account, one had only to strip naked and keep still in the sun. To Liu this seemed a very easy matter. If so small a thing would cure him, there was nothing better than to be cured. And, though he was not aware of it, he was also a little moved by curiosity at undergoing the barbarian monk's treatment.
student.ja: かう云ふ会話を繰返した末に、蛮僧は、簡単に、その療法を説明して聞かせた。――それによるに、唯、裸になつて、日向にぢつとしてゐさへすればよいと云ふのである。劉には、それが、甚、容易な事のやうに思はれた。その位の事で癒るなら、癒して貰ふのに越した事はない。その上、意識してはゐなかつたが、蛮僧の治療を受けると云ふ点で、好奇心も少しは動いてゐた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: So at last Liu bowed his head of his own accord, and it came to this: "Then I must ask you to cure me, if you please." — Such is the reason why Liu lies naked upon the threshing-floor in the blazing sun.
student.ja: そこでとうとう、劉も、こつちから頭を下げて、「では、どうか一つ、癒して頂きませう。」と云ふ事になつた。――劉が、裸で、炎天の打麦場にねころんでゐるのには、かう云ふ謂れが、あるのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Thereupon, saying he must not stir, the barbarian monk wound Liu's body round and round with thin cord. Then, bidding one of the servants, he had an unglazed earthen jar with wine in it brought to Liu's pillow. That Sun Sensei, the good friend of the wine-mound, should in the course of things have come to stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
student.ja: すると蛮僧は、身動きをしてはいけないと云ふので、劉の体を細引で、ぐるぐる巻にした。それから、僮僕の一人に云ひつけて、酒を入れた素焼の瓶を一つ、劉の枕もとへ持つて来させた。当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: What sort of thing the wine worm is, what happens when it is no longer in the belly, and what the jar of wine at the pillow is for, no one knows but the barbarian monk alone.
